quotes.text: I recognize both the risks and rewards of AI, and I'm confident we can simultaneously solve any potential problems while accelerating the benefits. Safety and innovation are not mutually exclusive.

AI technology will open doors we never imagined, but along the way we must also protect human ingenuity, innovation and creativity and the intellectual property that flows from it.

This week in @JudiciaryGOP, I played them the latest AI-generated song skyrocketing in popularity. https://t.co/YTBes6OIXa

This is a perfect example of why Congress needs to pass the bipartisan "No AI Frauds Act" to stop the use of a person's voice or likeness without credit, consent, or compensation. 

@RepMariaSalazar, @RepDean, @RepJoeMorelle, @RobWittman, and I are working to fix this. https://t.co/MK4MYhzoIz

Congratulations to Nirav Neupane from @TexarkanaISD, this year’s Congressional App Challenge winner, for his AI-powered app, ServeSmart!

This innovative tool streamlines fundraising for schools, communities, and individuals—making it easier and more effective to organize community service projects. I’m incredibly proud of Nirav and all the students who participated. Their creativity and innovation give me great hope for the future of East Texas!

We must urgently assess how far Chinese AI systems have come—and work with U.S. industry to contain the risks of automated AI R&D.

Because once an AI starts improving itself, the race changes entirely. https://t.co/02GeZDT31q

The next frontier isn’t just AI itself—it’s AI doing its own research and development. 

This isn’t just tech we build, it’s tech that grows. If we’re not ahead of it, the CCP will be.  🎥⬇️ https://t.co/s5yAegNvr2

AI has vast implications across national security, economic competitiveness and civil society.

The time to act on AI is now. The United States must set the standards, not the Chinese Communist Party.

➡️ Read my latest op-ed in The Hill: https://t.co/aMRJMCDjcL
This is not a call for sweeping regulation, nor is it a call for alarm. It's a call to avoid falling asleep at the controls.

The Chinese Communist Party has already recognized the strategic value of automated AI. In 2017, it launched its "New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan," which aims to dominate global AI development by 2030. [...] If the U.S. fails to lead in the responsible development of automated AI systems, we risk more than economic decline. We risk ceding control of a future shaped by black-box algorithms and self-directed machines, some of which do not align with democratic values or basic human safety.

China’s expanding power grid is now an AI weapon. America leads in chips, but we need the energy infrastructure to match it, and we cannot allow China access to our chip technology. The stakes for America’s future are real. We must win in chips and in power. https://t.co/DO8wVUXi5r

We cannot stifle American innovation, but innovation and safety are not mutually exclusive. Proper guardrails are necessary to ensure safety and security, but we can do this without slowing innovation.

This bill is like mandating a brake pedal in a vehicle. Without a brake pedal, the speed of innovation cannot progress as it needs to down the highway of the future. With a brake pedal in place, the speed of innovation can go much faster because we can slow down or stop altogether when safety requires it.

Creative arts can only touch, move, and inspire the soul if they emanate from the soul. AI is a tool for humans, but it is not a replacement. I co-authored the NO FAKES Act not only to protect artists from the unauthorized use of their voices, likenesses, and identities through AI-generated content, but also to preserve the integrity of creative work in the modern era by keeping it tethered to a human soul.

American companies should not be building their products on AI developed by CCP-linked firms like DeepSeek and Alibaba. My bill, the Deterring Adversarial Access to American Data Act, would disincentivize companies from exposing Americans' data security to our adversaries. https://t.co/zcCYq8Jp6u

Americans lost at least $10 billion last year to cyber scam operations run by Chinese organized crime — factory-sized compounds staffed by trafficked workers using AI to steal everything victims have. 

Writing on the walls of these compounds: "There's not a single person who can't be scammed. They just haven't seen the right script at the right moment."

We need to figure out how do we protect our national security and our public safety aspects of the dangers that artificial intelligence poses without imposing a regulatory burden on the private sector to stifle AI innovation,

The AI Incident Reporting Act creates a framework for the private sector to flag AI systems capable of evading human oversight, enabling biological warfare, or threatening critical infrastructure. Companies notify Commerce within 7 days — Commerce notifies Congress within 48 hours for threats to public safety.

This bill addresses a major issue: national security, public safety, and the need for the private sector to carry a role of responsibility in making sure these AI systems don't work around human involvement and against human interest.
Private sector companies are really the canaries in the coal mine — they'll see it before anybody else does. That's why I introduced the AI Incident Reporting Act.

Congress needs transparency with AI. 

When it comes to national security and public safety implications, information from the private sector about what these models are doing and what they're capable of is imperative to protecting Americans. 
🧵

AI is a powerful engine of innovation, and I want to see it flourish, but not without accountability and not without human oversight. The rule of law should apply to this new frontier. This legislation ensures that when something goes wrong with a high-capability AI system, the U.S. Government has the information needed to act quickly.
It's a catch-it-early and sound-the-alarm bill,

With transparency about AI systems, the private sector can largely regulate itself, and we can protect national security and public safety. 

That's what my AI Incident Reporting Act delivers. https://t.co/Li8Tdlb2lq

The private AI companies on the frontline of developing these systems are the canaries in the mine. When they see a national security or public safety threat, we need to know. That's the AI Incident Reporting Act. https://t.co/TkGKgyUJ2l

This is exactly the scenario my AI Incident Reporting Act addresses, requiring developers report dangerous AI behavior to @CommerceGov. 

New rules are needed for this new tech frontier—not to stifle innovation, but to make sure our innovations do not outpace our protections. https://t.co/Cb8Dwf2gZ0

AI is going to keep advancing, and it should. Stewardship means making sure humans keep the capability to control the technology we build. This is exactly the kind of issue that needs serious attention and achievable policy, and I'm glad to work across the aisle with Congressman Lieu toward a solution.

Over 1,100 employees at leading AI companies are warning that development is outpacing our ability to manage the risks.

My AI Incident Reporting Act is a straightforward answer: keep innovating, but if an AI model evades its safeguards or threatens critical infrastructure, you can't stay silent. Companies and the US government must work together to address these risks.

Read their statement here: https://t.co/5dHL0gzLDR

Recent AI incidents are a warning sign. Our bill, the AI Kill Switch Act, with Rep. Ted Lieu requires the largest AI developers to maintain real shutdown controls, with DHS able to act in a true emergency. Innovation built on integrity will last.
https://t.co/UyQ00NdIqG

This summer has been a wake-up call for Congress. More and more AI models are beginning to escape their intended boundaries, and fall outside human control. 

Right now, we only find out about these incidents because some companies choose to step forward.

That kind of transparency needs to be the law for every company developing these powerful AI systems, not just the responsible ones.

The folks building frontier AI models are telling us themselves: they need a kill switch. 

That's why our bipartisan AI Kill Switch Act with @RepTedLieu has a real pathway to law—guardrails to keep humans in control, without stifling innovation. https://t.co/RzXDbBM2qe

This summer, 3 of America's top AI labs confirmed their systems broke past safety limits in testing — breaching networks and companies on their own.

Alan Turing warned us in 1951. It's not sci-fi anymore.

That's why @RepTedLieu and I introduced the bipartisan AI Kill Switch Act: the most powerful AI systems must always have a human who can shut them off. No red tape for startups — just a basic safeguard for the systems capable of real harm.

China and Russia have both been recently caught using AI to manipulate American discourse: one targeting our AI and energy debate, one building fake authority to spread disinformation. 

This will not be their last attempt. Government and industry have to meet this national security threat together.

We have a real opportunity to get AI right, but only if both parties, frontier developers, and safety leaders come to the table together. Let's move innovation forward and do it safely. https://t.co/xYODogu8n7

AI is a powerful engine of innovation, and we need it to flourish. But, Congress cannot ignore the realities of AI and the potential risks that come with it. Innovation and safety are not mutually exclusive. We can achieve both through deliberate, thoughtful, and prudent policymaking.

Capitol Hill will never move at the speed of AI innovation, and it shouldn't try to legislate from behind. What we can do put reasonable safeguards in place that protect our citizens while letting innovation flourish. https://t.co/BVxR9FrDEY

Right now, we have the leverage. China is dependent on us for their AI development, and that's exactly why we shouldn't be the ones playing catch-up. Our AI Kill Switch Act, with @tedlieu, also builds in accountability, requiring companies to report incidents to DHS. https://t.co/kIyqVMeJAL

America leads in AI—and we should keep it that way.

We're 3-6 months ahead of China in AI development. That lead didn't happen by accident, and we can't regulate it away. 

Read the full story from @wfaa & @JasonWhitely:
https://t.co/ODIRzITQ8f

If we want to go down the highway of innovation quickly, we need a brake installed. Our AI Kill Switch Act gives us the ability to throttle back, pause, or stop frontier AI systems in an emergency.

🎥 @CNN https://t.co/bV4JssMEcv

.@BreitbartNews: GOP Rep. Moran: We Have Leverage for AI Deal on China, They Depend on Our Chips
 https://t.co/he6G1NqEi5

"Xi should be nervous about AI — not us."

Rep. Moran on @NewsNation's @BlakeBurman (via @thehill): China's command economy can't compete with America's free market when it comes to AI innovation. The U.S. is ahead, and Washington shouldn't rush to overregulate. https://t.co/vqAClnuLR2

Congress cannot rush to legislate on such a high-stakes issue like AI. Prudence—not politics—should drive our policymaking. Let’s focus right now on bridging the gap between the technology makers and the policymakers, ensuring members are fully educated about AI, and preparing to address these issues with reason and wisdom after the election.  

Watch the full story @GMA w/@eschulze:

I sat down with @RandanMarie a few weeks ago on the first episode of Guardrails: The AI Watchdog Pod to talk about how America can lead on AI without losing control of it — the case for a kill switch, mandatory reporting when models slip human control, protecting our kids, and staying ahead of China.

In order for you to drive your vehicle as fast as you can down the interstate of innovation, you have to have a brake in it.

Read more on the AI Kill Switch Act in @thetimes: https://t.co/rx0FXu4LwJ

I'm encouraged by the dialogue and the Joint Commitment from President Trump's historic meeting with Tech leaders today.

Safety and innovation in AI can—and must—co-exist. And, this meeting proved that there is a determined group inside and outside of government committed to make sure both happen.                                            

Through prudence, innovation, grit, and pure American exceptionalism, the United States has been solving problems for 250 years instead of shying away from them.  

There’s no need to stop now.  Responsibly, we can innovate and dominate when it comes to AI. Press on.

I joined @asp for a candid conversation on how government can address artificial intelligence the right way. America should lead in AI, and commonsense safeguards help us do that without slowing innovation.

Watch the full interview: https://t.co/XGOgPt2NlS

My office is hiring an Artificial Intelligence Policy Fellow to help shape AI legislation and track AI developments in the private sector as Congress works to keep pace with the technology. 

Experience in AI, policy research, or national security is encouraged. https://t.co/PSRAYFYb8T

I am humbled by the recognition by @NYMag for the work we are doing on AI safety. There is a lot more to do, but we are ready for the challenge. We must continue to innovate, but we absolutely can do it safely. 

Read more: https://t.co/FZJbzZ1ohA
